subject: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda

Team —

Kicking off coordination for Centauri's MSA/order form redlines around the security exhibit. Key points to resolve this week:

- Pen test notice and window (Centauri is asking for short notice but legal wants a minimum lead time).
- SOC 2 evidence delivery timeline and which artifacts we will provide vs. redacted copies.
- Staging access: ephemeral creds, scope of systems allowed (staging vs. prod), and sampling rules.
- Order form language: carveouts for scheduled pen tests and an acceptance criteria clause for remediation timelines.

Attached: evidence-matrix-initial.xlsx (stub) — I sketched a first pass mapping of who owns each artifact and a proposed cadence (monthly sampling for access logs, quarterly pen-test windows).

Can Kimberly and Neha confirm legal/security positions on the following by EOD?
- Minimum notice (30/45/60 days) for a customer-initiated pen test or third-party assessment.
- Whether we can provide a redacted SOC 2 report and a list of alternate artifacts (runbooks, control summaries).

Marissa, can you loop in GTM/procurement contact at Centauri and offer a short calendar with two proposed testing windows (Nov 15–21, Dec 6–12)? I want to avoid back-and-forth on dates.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda

Logan —

Thanks for the summary and the matrix. A few legal redline positions up front (high level):

1) Notice: 45 days minimum for customer-initiated pen tests; 30 days may be acceptable for vendor-run assessments if we control the scope and remediation windows. We should avoid open-ended "inspection at any time" verbiage.

2) Scope: We should gate staging vs. prod access. Any prod-level penetration requires a signed narrow-scope addendum and privileged-access windows (MFA & just-in-time).

3) Evidence delivery: we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a signed attestation letter for the current 12-month period. We should not include raw logs unless there's a mutual NDA/escrow process.

4) Pen test clause: propose adding an explicit remediation SLA for critical/high findings ("response plan and remediation patching timeline: initial triage within 48 hours, mitigation plan within 10 business days, resolution or workaround within 45 days unless otherwise agreed").

Open question for security (Neha): do we accept customer-run penetration tests that are executed by a third party who may request privileged access? If so we should require a point-in-time access token and a signed rules-of-engagement doc.

I’ll attach a marked-up MSA excerpt by EOD.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Moore <alice.moore@centauri.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Li <jason.li@centauri.com>, procurement@centauri.com
Date: 2026-10-03T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda

Marissa / Logan —

Appreciate you driving this. A few items from Centauri's security and procurement teams:

- SOC 2: We require the full SOC 2 Type II report covering the most recent 12-month period. Redacted version is acceptable, but we need the full control testing period and auditor statement.
- Pen test notice: 30 days is our internal policy, but we can be flexible to match vendor constraints. We do require the ability to scope tests to specific environments and have a short escalation channel for high-severity findings.
- Staging access: we prefer a dedicated test account range and agreed sampling rules. Can Redwood provide ephemeral accounts with MFA and granular network restrictions?
- Evidence cadence: our security team prefers a baseline monthly evidence exchange for access logs and quarterly third-party assessment summaries.

Attached: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (redacted placeholder). Procurement will start paperwork after legal confirms the updated exhibit wording; Jason is copied to coordinate PO and contract signature.

Best —
Alice Moore
Director, Information Security — Centauri Health
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moore <alice.moore@centauri.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda

Thanks Alice — good context. Quick plan to keep momentum:

1) Kimberly will circulate marked MSA + exhibit redlines by EOD (will include remediation SLA language and narrow-scoping template).
2) Neha will draft an operational rules-of-engagement (ROE) for third-party pen tests and a staging access checklist (ephemeral creds, MFA, scope, contact on-call).
3) I'll propose two concrete windows to Centauri (Nov 15–21, Dec 6–12) and ask for a preferred option. If Centauri needs 30 days, Nov 15 still works for a Nov 16–21 execution with initial planning calls in mid-Oct.
4) Marissa, please confirm procurement contact and push DocuSign once legal signs off; I created a placeholder routing: https://docusign.net/Sign?d=0a1b2c3d4e
5) I'll open a Jira ticket for tracking (SUP-7832) and tag legal/security for required artifacts.

If nobody objects to the remediation SLA/notice positions above, I'll send the schedule and the DocuSign link to Alice and Jason this afternoon.

Cheers —
Logan
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alice Moore <alice.moore@centauri.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling pen test window and exhibit ops agenda

Confirming operational items from security:

- We accept customer-initiated third-party pen tests under the following conditions: signed ROE, 45-day notice for any production-scoped tests, 30-day for staging-only.
- Ephemeral creds: we will issue scoped, time-limited accounts with MFA; engineer on-call will be provided for the scheduled window.
- Evidence exchange: we will provide monthly access-log samples (redacted) and quarterly assessment summaries. Full raw logs require a separate legal/data transfer agreement.
- ROE and staging checklist: attached to this reply in the Jira ticket SUP-7832 (link posted in thread).

I'll follow up with the ROE doc and sample checklist by close of business today.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
